text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: primary-east1-gpu-pool utilization 98%, pending queue ~12.4k, autoscaler attempted scale+20 but received error 'QuotaExceeded: gpus.regional.quota' — starting pager to oncall

maya: oncall here, looking. paging SRE now.

samira: on it. seeing repeated 'provision_timeout' from autoscaler logs, also a flurry of large long-context requests hitting 'x-model-heavy' route.

liam: runtime note: x-model-heavy is the long-context 32k variant; cold KV-caches + large batch windows = big memory pressure. Are these customer bursts or a rollout?

neha: support: 3 customers reporting 429 + 504s in last 10m, enterprise tenants A and B are highest. Sending list in DM.

dave: product: no recent rollouts that should hit that model. rolling back wouldn't help if capacity is missing.

jake: infra check: quota backend returning 403 from cloud provider for region-east1 GPU quota increase. Quota request still pending from yesterday. Autoscaler respects provider limits so it refused to create.

maya: TL;DR — primary pool saturated, autoscaler blocked by provider quota. Need immediate spillover to secondary region and temporary throttles for low-priority traffic.

samira: Agreed. Steps I'm going to take: 1) set routing policy to allow cross-region spillover for routes flagged as spillable; 2) add temporary rate-limit on non-SLAd tiers; 3) escalate quota with provider but that's slow.

liam: How do we flip routing policy quickly? Is there an orchestration API?

jake: yes — routing control plane supports a 'force_spillover' flag per-route. I'll run a safe change to only affect 'x-model-heavy' and 'batch-embed' routes.

jake: running command now:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_API_TOKEN" \
  https://routing.redwood.internal/v1/policies/force_spillover \
  -d '{"region":"secondary-west1","routes":["/v1/generate/x-model-heavy","/v1/embeddings/batch-embed"],"duration_minutes":30}'
```

inc-bot: deploy-bot: routing policy change queued, started rollout to control-plane nodes (10/12). :white_check_mark:

maya: staging a rate-limit change for non-paid tiers to reduce pressure. Samira, can we limit to 1 rps per token for low-tier?

samira: yes. applying token-level limiter patch:
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate/*","policy":{"priority_filter":"low","max_rps":1}}
```

inc-bot: rate-limiter change applied across edge (completed).

neha: customers A and B reporting some reduction in errors, latency still high for heavy requests. They're asking for ETA — what do we tell them?

maya: tell them we're actively failing over heavy workloads to secondary region and throttling low-priority requests. ETA for visible improvements ~5-10m after spillover completes.

liam: runtime logs show KV-cache misses spiking in secondary too as requests start to arrive; we should enable prefix caching fallback to reduce cold starts. Pushing a config to enable aggressive prefix_cache for x-model-heavy (ttl 10m).

liam: pushing config:
```yaml
route: /v1/generate/x-model-heavy
cache:
  prefix_cache: true
  ttl_seconds: 600
  max_entries: 50000
```

samira: manual intervention: added a temporary reservation of 8 GPUs from reserved pool in west1 for high-priority tenants. Note: that reduces our pool for other regions.

jake: routing rollout at 12/12 nodes, spillover live to secondary-west1. Confirming traffic cutover metrics.

inc-bot: metric-alert: queue length primary-east1 decreased from 12.4k -> 1.1k in 6m after spillover; secondary-west1 GPU utilization jumped to 75%.

maya: good. how are we on customer visible errors? Neha?

neha: enterprise A reports 80% success on heavy requests now (previously 30%). Enterprise B still seeing intermittent 504s for very large contexts.

samira: digging into 504s — seeing some model-variant negotiation failures when routing to secondary due to model-variant mismatch (primary had v3-legacy, secondary has v3-quant). I'm enabling variant-fallback in runtime so that compatible quantized variant can be used automatically.

liam: applying variant fallback flag (allow_compatible_variant=true) for x-model-heavy. This will reshuffle KV caches briefly.

inc-bot: runtime-bot: variant-fallback toggle accepted; warming caches for compatible variants started.

jake: provider quota team finally replied — they can open +40 GPUs but it will take 2 hours to provision. We'll still want the permanent change but not immediate.

maya: current mitigations: 1) spillover enabled to secondary-west1, 2) low-tier rate-limits applied, 3) reserved-pool emergency allocation of 8 GPUs, 4) variant-fallback on for heavy model, 5) prefix_cache enabled. Observed effect: overall queue down 90%, errors down ~60% for most customers.

dave: customer impact note: some enterprise tenants experienced degraded throughput and higher token latency for 12m, a few requests retried client-side. We'll coordinate a message.

neha: drafting customer comms now — will note mitigation steps, impacted time window, and we will follow up with root cause and timeline.

maya: okay team, next steps:
- Jake: confirm reserved pool refill and track provider quota provision (follow up in infra channel)
- Samira & Liam: root cause triage on autoscaler refusal path and variant mismatch; reproduce in staging
- Dev: determine if we can add proactive early-detection alert when autoscaler receives provider quota errors (new alert rule)
- Neha & Dave: finalize customer comms and CM ticket

samira: quick note — autoscaler path: it retries create -> provider returns 'QuotaExceeded' -> autoscaler interprets as transient and backs off for 10m. We'll need to treat 'QuotaExceeded' as hard failure and trigger immediate spillover in future. Filing a ticket now.

liam: filed infra/regression ticket: INF-4821 — autoscaler quota error handling. Also created runtime ticket: RUNTIME-3298 for variant compatibility mapping gaps.

maya: any objections to keeping force_spillover flag active for 60 more minutes while provider quota fills?

jake: no objections. I'll increase duration to 90m to be safe.

inc-bot: incident-note: mitigation checklist completed, monitoring for secondary saturation. Paging will remain open until primary queue < 500 and all high-priority customer errors under 2%.

neha: customer comms ready, sending after Maya approval.

maya: approved. Thanks all. I'll do a handoff to next oncall in 40m.

samira: tagging follow-ups for postmortem: autoscaler error classification, quota automation runbook, model-variant parity checklist, better spillover smoke tests.

maya: closing remarks: great quick work. After-action: schedule 1h incident review with infra + runtime + support tomorrow.

jake: updated infra channel with provider ticket link and reserved pool numbers.

inc-bot: incident resolved? condition: primary queue now at 420, high-priority errors <1.5% -> threshold met. Marking incident as 'mitigated' and leaving for oncall handoff. :white_check_mark:

maya: handing off to next oncall @samira in 40m, will append notes to the ticket.

neha: will attach customer logs to CM ticket and send comms.

samira: acknowledged, will monitor overnight.

maya: thanks team.
